Implementation Plan

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends `_mt_find_marker_comment_id`
Scope-mode justification: The finding names one trust gap: `scripts/review_merge_train.sh` treats any comment that starts with `<!-- merge-train:queued -->` as queue state the train wrote itself, no matter who posted it. A second weakness feeds it: the bypass still goes ahead when consuming that marker fails. The fix stays inside that boundary. The existing marker lookup will only accept comments by the account the train authenticates as (`GH_PAT`, resolved once per run through `GET /user`). The one-shot bypass will only proceed once that verified marker has actually been consumed. Release, upsert and label handling get the same author filter for free because they already go through the one lookup helper. Workflow wiring, label policy and the fail-open contract for API errors stay as they are. Per §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the extra cost is one identity read and a few lines of shell, and it closes the hole fully rather than adding a heuristic. So the complete fix is the right choice and nothing is reduced.

**Planning ref:** `git rev-parse HEAD` = `4ffff46d8100bea12bfb77df17e3886a18bf2748`, branch `ai/issue-4701`. That matches the integration branch metadata, so there is no mismatch. The dependency #6500 (fork PRs cannot block the train) is already on this branch; see `changelog.d/6500-merge-train-fork-blockers.md`.

**Automation / scheduler surface (§20.E)**
- **Script status:** extends an existing script, `scripts/review_merge_train.sh`. No new script, workflow or supervisor.
- **Entry points (unchanged):**
  - `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, step "Merge-train gate", runs on `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` with `GH_TOKEN: secrets.GH_PAT`.
  - `.github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml`, merge-train release, runs on `pull_request.closed` and the `*/5` schedule with `GH_TOKEN: GH_PAT || GITHUB_TOKEN`.
  - `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`, merge-train release backstop, runs on every poll tick with `GH_PAT`.
- **Long-running supervisor:** none needed.
- **DB work:** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`:** no entry, since nothing new is introduced.

---

**1. Files likely to change**
- `scripts/review_merge_train.sh`: the fix.
- `tests/test_review_merge_train.py`: changes to the fake `gh`, the existing comment fixtures, and new regression tests.
- `README.md`:
  - The `MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED` row (line ~119).
  - The merge-train `gate` table row (line ~2401).
  - In both, say that only a marker written by the pipeline account counts as queue state.
- `agents.md`: one sentence in the review-autofix "merge train" bullet (phase 7) saying the queued marker is verified against the `GH_PAT` account.
- `changelog.d/6501-merge-train-marker-author.md`: new fragment with the `<!-- changelog: security -->` heading, same shape as the 6500 fragment.

No workflow YAML changes, so §24 file size is not affected.

**2. Functions / modules to implement**

All in `scripts/review_merge_train.sh`.

a. **New globals**, defined next to the `MT_*` constants. I grepped the script and the names are unused.
   - `_MT_MARKER_AUTHOR=""`
   - `_MT_MARKER_AUTHOR_STATE=""`, taking the values `""`, `ok` or `failed`.

b. **New `_mt_resolve_marker_author()`.** It must always be called in the parent shell, never inside `$(...)`, so the cache survives.
   - If the state is already `ok`, return 0. If it is `failed`, return 1. So there is at most one call per run.
   - Otherwise run `gh_retry gh api user --jq '.login // ""'`.
   - Accept the login only if it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}(\[bot\])?$`. This guarantees it is safe to interpolate into the `--jq` string literal.
   - On success, set the login and state `ok`. On failure, set state `failed`, emit `_mt_warn "merge-train: could not resolve the authenticated account; queue markers are unverifiable this run."` and return 1.
   - Add a §14 comment above the call. It should say that the existing open-PR listing, files and comments calls were audited, none of them returns the token's identity, and this is the same `gh api user` probe that `review_rb_judge_security_pass.sh` and `review_single_issue_security_pass.sh` use.

c. **Change `_mt_find_marker_comment_id()`** at line 272.
   - If `_MT_MARKER_AUTHOR_STATE != ok`, return 1 (lookup failure). It never falls back to accepting any author.
   - The jq filter becomes `.[] | select(.user.login == "<author>" and (.body | startswith("<marker>"))) | .id`. Keep the latest match with `tail -n 1`.
   - Update the comment: comments from other authors are ignored because anyone who can comment could forge one, which is the `forged-queue-comment-bypasses-train` finding.

d. **Change `_mt_gate()`:**
   - **Unblocked path with the label present** (before line 355): call `_mt_resolve_marker_author || true` before the lookup. On lookup failure the existing behaviour keeps the label for the release backstop.
   - **Blocked path** (before line 373): call `_mt_resolve_marker_author || true`. If the lookup fails (API or identity), keep the existing branch: warn and fail open, not queued. That is the documented contract, and an attacker cannot trigger it.
   - **Bypass branch** (lines 377–383), when the label is absent and there is a verified marker ID:
     - Consume the marker with `_mt_replace_comment "${queued_comment_id}" "${MT_BYPASSED_MARKER}…"`.
     - Only if that succeeds, log `result=bypassed` and return 0.
     - If it fails, warn "could not consume the one-shot bypass marker for PR #N; keeping it queued" and fall through to the normal queue path. That path re-adds the label, upserts the marker and soft-exits. This removes the "this run still proceeds" behaviour.
   - **Queue path:** the upsert keeps receiving `queued_comment_id`. That value now always points to the pipeline's own comment, so a forged comment is never edited. If there is no ID, a fresh comment is posted.

e. **Change `_mt_release()`.** Before the queue-marker lookup (line ~697), call `_mt_resolve_marker_author || true` in the loop body; the loop runs in the parent shell (`done < <(...)`). If identity fails, the existing branch applies: warn and leave the PR queued. This is needed because removing the label while a pipeline-authored marker is still live would look like a human bypass. A release run with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (no `GH_PAT`, where `/user` returns 403) therefore defers to the `GH_PAT` poll backstop. The released-comment upsert inherits the author filter automatically.

f. **Header "API budget" block.**
   - Gate: +1 `GET /user` when blockers exist or the queue label is present.
   - Release: +1 `GET /user` per invocation, and only when a queued PR reaches the marker step.
   - Note under the fail-open contract that an unresolvable identity counts as a marker-lookup failure.

**3. Data structures affected**
- No schema changes.
- The `<!-- merge-train:queued|bypassed|queue-retired|released -->` marker strings are unchanged.
- The meaning of "queue state" narrows to markers authored by the pipeline account.
- Gate log keys (`MERGE_TRAIN_GATE … result=bypassed|queued`) are unchanged.

**4. API / interface changes**
- No CLI, env-var or output changes.
- New GitHub API read: `GET /user`, at most once per run.
- No new env vars, so §8 does not apply. The helper keeps working under `review_autofix.yml@main` staging because it needs no new export.

---

## Decisions

### D1 — Authenticate markers by comment author, not by content
- **Chosen:** Accept a marker only when `.user.login` equals the login behind the run's `GH_TOKEN` (`GET /user`), applied inside `_mt_find_marker_comment_id` so gate, release and upsert all share it.
- **Alternatives considered:** Sign or HMAC the marker body (needs a secret, which the scripts don't have). Accept `author_association` OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR (a collaborator could still forge, and the bot account's association varies by repo). Hard-code `github-actions[bot]` (wrong: the gate writes as the `GH_PAT` account).
- **Why:** The bypass is only meant to be armed by the train's own writes. Author identity is set by GitHub and cannot be forged by a commenter. The same pattern already exists for `REVIEW_AUTOFIX_PARTIAL_V1` and the single-issue security-pass markers.

### D2 — Bypass only after the verified marker is consumed
- **Chosen:** If the PATCH that turns the marker into `merge-train:bypassed` fails, the PR is re-queued instead of proceeding.
- **Alternatives considered:** Keep "this run still proceeds". That leaves the marker armed and makes the bypass repeatable.
- **Why:** The finding asks for a "verified, authorized queue-state transition". A bypass that can't be recorded is not a completed transition. Failing closed only delays the review; it never blocks a merge.

### D3 — Identity failure is treated as a lookup failure
- **Chosen:** Reuse the existing lookup-failure branches. The gate's blocked path fails open (not queued). The unblocked path and release keep the label.
- **Alternatives considered:** Fall back to accepting any author (reintroduces the bug). Make the blocked-path fail closed (queue) on any API error (contradicts the documented fail-open contract, out of scope).
- **Why:** An attacker cannot cause either failure. It keeps the existing contract and is the smallest change.

### D4 — No label-event actor verification
- **Chosen:** Rely on GitHub's own authorization for removing the label (triage or higher). Do not read issue events to check who removed it.
- **Alternatives considered:** Fetch the `unlabeled` event and check the actor's permission (+1 to 2 API calls per gate).
- **Why:** Once forged markers are ignored, the only way left to trigger a bypass is a label removal by someone with repo permission, which is the documented human bypass. Extra calls would add API load (§14) for no security gain.
